reasoning_content:
There's a circle with center O and diameter AB (horizontal line). Angles shown: 30° between OB and some ray (going toward lower-left), 65° between that ray and another ray, 40° between... let me look at the figure.

The diameter AB is horizontal: B on left, A on right. From O, rays going downward: one ray to lower-left (boundary of shaded sector), one ray to lower-left-ish steep (another boundary of shaded sector), one ray to lower-right.

Angles marked: 30° between OB (leftward horizontal) and the first ray (lower-left direction, boundary of shaded region). Actually, the 30° label is between the OB line and the ray going to lower-left (around point (120, 500)). The arc for 30° is between OB and that ray.

Then 65° is between the two rays: the steep lower-left ray (boundary of shaded sector, red line) and the lower-right ray? Wait, the 65° arc is between the red ray (steep, going down to (290, 630)) and the ray going to lower-right (390, 540)? Hmm.

Let me set up coordinates: O at center (approx (360, 360) in image coordinates). A on right (635, 360). B on left (82, 360).

Rays from O:
- To B: angle 180°.
- Ray to (120, 500): direction lower-left. Angle: vector (120-360, 500-360) = (-240, 140). In standard math coordinates (y up), image y is down, so math coords: (-240, -140). Angle = atan2(-140, -240) ≈ 180+30 = 210°? atan2(-140,-240): reference angle atan(140/240)=30.25°, third quadrant: 180+30.25=210.25°, i.e., -150°. So angle from OB (180°) is 30° downward. Yes, matches 30° label between OB and this ray.

- Red ray to (290, 630): vector (-70, 270) image => math (-70, -270). Angle: atan2(-270, -70) = 180+75.5 = 255.5°, i.e., -104.5°? Hmm atan(270/70)=75.5°, third quadrant: 180+75.5=255.5° (measured counterclockwise from positive x-axis). Equivalent to -104.5°.

- Ray to (570, 540): vector (210, 180) image => math (210, -180). Angle = atan2(-180, 210) = -40.6°. So 40° below OA (positive x-axis). Matches 40° label between OA and this ray.

- 65° label at (400, 460): between red ray (255.5° i.e., -104.5°) and ray at -40.6°? Difference: -40.6 - (-104.5) = 63.9 ≈ 65°. Yes, the 65° arc is between the red ray and the lower-right ray.

Shaded sector: between ray at 210° (i.e., -150°) and red ray at -104.5°: difference ≈ 45.5°. Hmm, but let me compute exactly: angles around O on lower side: from OB (180°) going clockwise (downward): 30° to first ray, then shaded sector angle x, then 65° to next ray, then 40° to OA. Total on lower side of diameter = 180°. So 30 + x + 65 + 40 = 180 => x = 45°.

Therefore shaded sector angle = 45°. Probability = 45/360 = 1/8.

Wait, but the shaded sector is between the 30° ray and the red ray: yes, shaded region boundaries: ray to (120,500) and red ray to (290,630), with arc between them. So central angle = 180 - 30 - 65 - 40 = 45°.

Probability = 45/360 = 1/8.

Thus answer: \boxed{1/8}.

Double-check: sum of angles on straight line AB (lower half) = 180°. Angles: 30° (between OB and ray1), shaded angle (between ray1 and ray2), 65° (between ray2 and ray3), 40° (between ray3 and OA). Sum = 180 => shaded = 45°. Probability = 45/360 = 1/8.

Thus answer \boxed{1/8}.
content:
Looking at the lower half of the circle (below diameter AB), the angles around O on that side must sum to 180°.

The angles are: 30° (between OB and the first ray), the shaded sector's angle, 65°, and 40°.

Shaded angle = 180° − 30° − 65° − 40° = 45°.

Probability = (shaded sector area)/(disk area) = 45°/360° = 1/8.

\boxed{1/8}
